To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of a novel microtiter plate format with a new method for the immobilization of allergens on solid phase, and a new IgE‐detection method, allows the investigation of IgE reactivity profiles of large numbers of sera against a large panel of allergens in a short time, with high capacity.
we have developed an efficient method for the investigation of IgE reactivity profiles using allergen arrays.
the use of recombinant allergen arrays allows for fast and simple IgE reactivity profiling of allergenic sources.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of allergens and allergen components.
developing new methods for the investigation of IgE reactivity profiles.
the development of new methods for allergen analysis and the characterization of allergen sources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of recombinant allergen microarrays is not yet a standard tool in the clinical laboratory for the diagnosis and management of patients with IgE‐mediated allergy.

there are no differences in the IgE reactivity of patients with asthma, allergic rhinitis or atopic dermatitis, but the differences in IgE binding patterns between the different patient groups are more subtle than expected.
there is no evidence to show that the IgE‐reactivities of the different recombinant allergen preparations differ significantly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to perform an arrayed IgE‐reactivities investigation of up to 24 allergens on a single 96‐well microtitre plate.
we have developed a simple, robust and fast method for the analysis of IgE reactivity profiles using natural and purified recombinant allergen extracts.

the combination of the two methods described in this article is a powerful tool for the analysis of the IgE‐binding profile of allergen extracts and for the characterization of recombinant allergen preparations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of the microarray platform and the use of recombinant proteins is a very promising tool for allergen‐specific immunotherapy.

the combination of a simple microtiter plate‐based method and the use of a large panel of recombinant and natural allergens allows the identification of IgE reactivity profiles of patients with allergic diseases.

we have established a rapid, easy‐to‐handle, high‐throughput method for arraying allergen extracts, recombinant allergen proteins, or allergen peptides on nitrocellulose membrane and for detecting specific IgE binding.
